facts.statement: Pluridens imelaki lived during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian age.
The type locality of Pluridens imelaki is Upper Couche III in Morocco.
facts.quote:
Type locality: Upper Couche III
Country: Morocco

facts.statement: Pluridens imelaki is known from a single skull and associated lower jaws discovered in Moroccan phosphates.
facts.quote: A fourth species, Pluridens imelaki, was also described from the same phosphates of Morocco in 2026 based on a single skull and associated lower jaws.

facts.statement: Pluridens species possessed very long, slender dentaries with a nearly circular cross‑section toward the tip.
facts.quote: Very long, slender dentary, anterior half cross-section almost circular extending to tip.

facts.statement: Pluridens individuals could reach 5–6 m in length, with some specimens possibly exceeding 9 m.
facts.quote: measuring 5 - 6 m long and perhaps over 9 m in some individuals

facts.statement: The jaws of some Pluridens specimens are robust and display injuries that suggest combat, possibly over mates or territories.
facts.quote: The jaws in some specimens are robust, and sometimes show injuries suggestive of combat. The jaws may have been used for fighting over mates or territories.

facts.statement: Pluridens was initially considered for a separate subfamily because of its unique high tooth count and tooth shape, but it is now placed within the Halisaurinae.
facts.quote: the genus to be firmly placed within the Halisaurinae

facts.statement: Pluridens imelaki had a skull measuring 1.25 m, indicating a total body length of about 9 m or more.
The species possessed roughly 25 teeth in the dentary.
Pluridens imelaki was exceptionally rare in the Moroccan phosphates, known from only a single specimen among hundreds of mosasaur remains.
Pluridens imelaki lived during the Maastrichtian stage, about 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The species belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
Only one fossil occurrence of Pluridens imelaki has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
